candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — toddler choking prevention
candidate.educational_objective: Teach caregivers to reduce toddler choking risk through developmentally appropriate food preparation, avoidance of common choking hazards, seated eating, and direct supervision.

options.A: Offer hard candy and whole nuts as routine snacks because these foods help strengthen chewing skills.
options.B: Serve whole grapes and round hot-dog slices because chewing is mature enough once a toddler can walk.
options.C: Allow the child to eat while walking or playing because movement does not meaningfully affect choking risk.
options.D: Prepare foods in developmentally appropriate shapes, sizes, and textures, avoid small hard or round hazards, and have the child sit while eating under close supervision.

candidate.rationale: CDC choking-prevention guidance recommends preparing food in a shape, size, and texture appropriate for the child's development; avoiding small, sticky, or hard foods; having the child sit while eating rather than walk or crawl; and supervising the child at all times during meals. Whole grapes, hot dogs/sausages, whole or chopped nuts, and hard candy are listed as potential choking hazards. D combines the supported prevention measures; A through C increase risk.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CDC recommends developmentally appropriate food shape/size/texture, avoiding small hard choking hazards, seated eating, and continuous supervision; whole grapes, hot dogs, nuts, and hard candy are listed choking hazards.
candidate.source_document_title: Choking Hazards — Infant and Toddler Nutrition
